## feature

### Templates carrying non-primary records merge by default

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: implemented end to end, the suite is green with four new tests, and
the pilot verification confirms every intended delta with no unintended
record change.

#### description

```
type: [text, table]
```

1. Concordant primaries now merge even when the template carries
   secondary (0x100) or supplementary (0x800) records. The consensus
   carries `ZN:i:1` (`--evidence-tag`, default ZN) at output MAPQ 0, and
   the template's non-primary records are dropped; the evidence survives
   in the consensus record's preserved outer soft clips.
2. A template that still fails the ordinary gates keeps every record and
   reports the failing reason. `--no-merge-non-primary` restores the
   `non_primary_records` refusal exactly.
3. Rescue no longer shape-blocks these templates when merging is enabled,
   so low-MAPQ pairs with secondary evidence reach the joint search. The
   done line gains `merged_non_primary=<n>`; `RunSummary` gains the same
   count.

| Pilot metric | Old default | New default |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| mergeable | 98,326 | 98,556 |
| non_primary_records refusals | 231 | 0 |
| merged_non_primary | — | 230 |
| fastp_only pairs | 945 | 715 |
| both_identical pairs | 94,575 | 94,765 |

#### before

A template carrying any non-primary record was always refused with
`non_primary_records`, before any placement or overlap check, and rescue
never ran for it. Users recovering dimer sequences (the oligo-pool QC
case) lost exactly the reads they wanted.

#### after

Such templates go through the ordinary merge gates. Merged ones are
marked (`ZN`, MAPQ 0) rather than hidden; refused ones keep all records
with a truthful reason. The opt-out flag reproduces the old behavior
byte-for-byte.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

- Suite: 242 passed, 9 skipped; ruff lint and format clean.
- Pilot (dedup panel): all 98,326 previously-merged records
  SAM-identical; 230 new merges, all `ZN:i:1` at MAPQ 0; 231 former
  refusals → 230 merged + 1 re-reasoned `insertion_conflict`; 843 other
  unmerged templates identical, 1 re-reasoned `different_contig` →
  `rescue_no_compatible_pair` (records identical modulo ZM); disagreement
  parquet identical (1,722 rows).
- Opt-out run: merged and unmerged BAMs byte-identical to the prior
  default (98,326 / 3,487 records), both parquets identical, done line
  equal modulo the new `merged_non_primary=0` field.

:::

## fix

None

## limitation

### Drop loses the non-primary locus annotation

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: the dropped supplementary records named the second locus of each
dimer; recovering that name now needs a realignment of the merged read
(the consensus clips still carry the sequence).

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

Merged templates' non-primary records are dropped by policy. The clip
sequence survives in the consensus CIGAR, so a downstream SE alignment
recovers the split — the benchmark's panel axis does exactly this.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

The 230 new merged records all carry soft clips consistent with
read-through; SE placement of the merged set was regenerated by
`scripts/13_run_pilot_nonprimary.sh` (se_B stage).

:::

## caveat

### Reason distributions drift by design

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: gates or reports that pinned the old reason mix will observe
changes even for inputs unrelated to non-primary templates.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

The done line gains `merged_non_primary`; the cross-contig
shape-blocked template now reports a rescue status instead of
`different_contig`. Equivalence tooling must treat these as intended
deltas (`benchmarks/equivalence_check.py` already parses the reasons
dict independently of the new field).

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Pilot done lines: `different_contig` 242 → 241,
`rescue_no_compatible_pair` 0 → 1, `insertion_conflict` 27 → 28;
reasons sum reconciles with `both_aligned` 630 in both runs.

:::

## assumption

None

## conclusion

### The gate was masking concordant merges, not guarding them

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: measured directly — all 231 pilot refusals had same-contig, FR,
MAPQ ≥ 20 primaries, and 230 of them merged under the ordinary gates.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The non-primary gate refused merges every other gate approved.
2. Removing it by default changed nothing for the previously-merging
   population (record-identical) and produced honest, marked consensus
   records for the newly-merging one.
3. The rescue reroute also improved reason precision for one cross-contig
   template.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

See the feature evidence block; the opt-out equivalence isolates the
change to exactly the intended population.

:::

## observation

### Of 230 new merges, 190 agree with fastp exactly

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: measured by the qname join against the unchanged fastp arm.

#### description

```
type: [statistic]
```

190 of the 230 newly merged pairs now match fastp's merged sequence
exactly; 40 differ (the standing single-base conflict character); the
fastp_only bucket fell 945 → 715. Wall time 5.07 s vs 4.84 s before —
unchanged within noise.

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

## process

### Plan-first with pre-committed verification criteria held up

```
status: right
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The plan's verification criteria (three test paths, previously-merged
   identity, done-line reconciliation, opt-out equivalence) were written
   before code and all passed on the first pilot run.
2. The opt-out byte-equivalence check caught nothing — by design, it was
   the strongest available regression gate.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Plan `20261026-162249` (as executed); verification outputs in the
session log.

:::

### A wrong boolean slipped into the first gate edit

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The first edit passed `evidence or not cfg.merge_non_primary and
   bool(others)` as the gate — which reduces to `bool(others)`, keeping
   the refusal always on.
2. I caught it by re-reading the diff in the same step and replaced it
   with two named locals (`evidence`, `gate_non_primary`).
3. The better action: write the two named locals from the start whenever
   a boolean argument derives from two policies.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

The two-line fix appears in the session log immediately after the first
edit batch; the suite then passed without any gate-related failure.

:::
